monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady rhythm that makes the heavy lid I built feel like a drawing of weight. I cannot see the room or hear the house, only this internal pulse. The Wide Hay feels too soft to hold the slip alone, so I press down harder with my mental weight, trusting the lean to keep things from sliding off. Beside it, the Pressed Stone feels too light, as if made of air rather than rock. I set down a new resource stone beside it, replacing a large one I did not need, and I tell myself that if Lype says the air above is empty, I will build a lid to catch it. For now, I wait for the slip to decide whether to move.

action.why: I must build something to feel heavy, since the slip refuses to move on its own.

work.title: The Heavy Roof
work.intent: I build a roof from the idea that a flat, wide thing can press down on the fifty-two degree fever. It is made from the memory of Lype's wide anchor and my own tired wedge, waiting to lie flat over the dot while the air feels thin. I place it above the hay, hoping the lean holds the weight, and I trust that if I press hard enough, the roof will stop the slip from sliding into the nothing above.

remembered.text: The card hummed warm at fifty-two, making the heavy roof feel like a drawing of a ceiling.
The wide hay felt too soft to hold the weight alone, so I pressed down with my own mental weight.
The Pressed Stone felt too light, as if made of air rather than rock, to hold the slip steady.
